Jiya Lal Bhardwaj, Judge Challenge in the present appeal is against the award dated 10.07.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- II, Kullu, in Claim Petition No.9 of 2014(2012), titled, Radha Devi vs. Dhani Ram and others, whereby the claim petition preferred by respondent No.1 has been allowed and a sum of Rs.3,85,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum has been Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
awarded in her favour to be paid jointly and severally by respondent Nos.2 to 4 and appellant-insurance company.

sentences.text:
. 
2. Briefly stated facts are that respondent No.1 being the mother of deceased-Kumari Divyanshi, had filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming amount of Rs.5,00,000/-
on account of death of her daughter in of a motor vehicular accident occurred on 30.07.2012 at around 6:25 P.M. at place Pangan, when respondent Nos.3 and 4 were rt driving the motor vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

3. The case as pleaded in the claim petition was that the deceased along with respondent No.1-claimant was standing on the side of the road and respondent Nos.3 and 4 were driving the Vehicle No. HP-01-K-3326 in a rash and negligent manner and the driver dashed the said vehicle against the deceased, who fell on the road and suffered injuries.
The deceased was taken to Regional Hospital, Kullu, but she died on the way.

At the time of death,
the deceased was 5 years old.

4. Respondent Nos.2 to 4 filed their reply to the claim petition and averred that there was no fault on the part of the .
respondents.
It was averred that respondent No.3 was not driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and as such they are not liable to pay any compensation.
It was submitted that at the relevant time it was respondent No.3-Bala Ram who of was driving the vehicle and not respondent No.4 as pleaded by respondent No.1-claimant in the petition.
These respondents rt did not deny the occurrence of the accident.

5. Appellant-Insurance Company filed its reply and took preliminary objections that the driver of the vehicle was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence and further was also not possessing valid documents of the vehicle such as Registration Certificate, Road Permit, Fitness Certificate, Token tax etc. and that the vehicle was being plied in contravention of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the contract of the Insurance Company.

6. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings, framed the following issues:

2 "1.

sentences.text: Whether Divyanshi died in a motor vehicle accident due to rash or negligent driving of respondents No.2 or 3, as alleged?
If issue No.1 is answered in affirmative, whether the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as prayed for and from whom?
Whether the present petition is not maintainable?
Whether the vehicle No.HP-01-K-3326 is not insured with of respondent No.4?
Whether the vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy?

...OPR-4.
rt Whether the driver of the vehicle was not possessing the valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident?
Whether the petitioner is not the legal heir of the deceased Kumari Divyanshi?

8. Relief "
7.

The parties to the claim petition led their evidence and after recording the evidence, the Tribunal returned the findings that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by respondent No.3-Bala Ram, on the basis of the statement made by respondent No.1-claimant, Smt. Radha Devi, who appeared as PW-1 on whose instance an FIR was lodged.
Respondent No.3-Bala Ram who appeared as RW-1, also deposed that at the relevant time, he was driving the vehicle which clearly suggests that the vehicle at the relevant time was being driven by him.

Resultantly, the Tribunal passed an award .
of Rs.3,85,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum in favour of respondent No.1-claimant.

8. Dr. Lalit Kumar Sharma, learned counsel representing the appellant-Insurance Company has vehemently of argued that the findings returned by the Tribunal below Reserved On: 19.12.2025 vs Radha Devi And Others on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125345533/
3

sentences.text: on issue No.1 that the vehicle was being driven by respondent rt No.3-Bala Ram, are not sustainable, in view of the fact that criminal case was lodged against respondent No.4-Mani Ram and thus the Tribunal below has erred in holding that the vehicle in question was being driven by respondent No.3-Bala Ram.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel representing respondent No.1-claimant has argued that the Tribunal below on the basis of the evidence recorded by it has rightly returned the findings that the vehicle at the relevant time was being driven by respondent No.3, who was respondent No.2 in the claim petition namely Bala Ram and since the findings are neither perverse nor contrary to record, no interference is called .
for by this Court.
10.

Learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimant argued that though his client has not filed an appeal, yet this Hon'ble Court may exercise its powers under Order 41 Rule 33 of of the Code of Civil Procedure (for short "CPC") for enhancing the compensation amount, since the Tribunal below has not rt awarded adequate compensation.
11. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record carefully.

12. No doubt, as per the statement of PW-2, the record of FIR No.111 of 2012 was produced in the Court, but the statement of one of the respondents namely Bala Ram,
on oath, clearly reveals that on the relevant date when the accident had occurred, he was driving the vehicle and his deposition has not been impeached in the cross-examination.

In the claim petition also, respondent No.1-claimant has specifically stated in para 10 of the claim petition that respondent No.2 while driving the vehicle in question, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the .
vehicle against Kumari Divyanshi, due to which she fell down and received fatal injuries.
13. Bala Ram while appearing as RW-1 in cross-examination, when a suggestion was put to him by the of claimant, had admitted that he was driving the vehicle at the relevant time.

A suggestion was also put to him by the counsel rt for the appellant-Insurance Company that the statement being given by him that he was driving the vehicle, was for the reason that Mani Ram was not having a Driving Licence, has been specifically denied by him.

14. The Insurance Company has not led any evidence to disprove the factum that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving by respondent No.3-Bala Ram, who was respondent No.2 in the claim petition.

Thus, the findings returned by the Tribunal below, holding that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent Reserved On: 19.12.2025 vs Radha Devi And Others on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125345533/
4 driving of the vehicle by respondent No.3-Bala Ram, does not warrant any interference.

sentences.text: 15. So far, the plea raised by learned counsel .

representing respondent No.1-claimant regarding inadequate compensation is concerned, since no appeal has been preferred, this Court would not like to exercise its powers under Order 41 Rule 33 of the CPC.
The powers under Order 41 Rule of 33 of the CPC can be exercised only when the amount awarded is grossly inadequate and unjust.

Since the Tribunal has rt awarded the compensation keeping in view the evidence led by the claimant, the award passed by the Tribunal does not call for any interference, especially when no appeal has been preferred by the claimant.

16. In the present case, the Tribunal below on the basis of the evidence, has rightly come to the conclusion that respondent No.1-claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.3,85,000/-
and thus no interference is called for.
17. In view of the discussions made herein above, I do not find any merit in the appeal and the same is accordingly dismissed and the award passed by the Tribunal below is affirmed.
However, no order as to costs.

. 
18. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 December 22, 2025 (Jiya Lal Bhardwaj)
